title: Cross-SDK streaming retry contract tests and deterministic mockserver examples
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: Create a portable, deterministic mockserver and a set of cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) example suites that validate streaming ergonomics, retry semantics, and contract expectations against the Redwood API. This ticket covers the mockserver design, fixture format, example test harnesses, CI integration, and acceptance criteria for production-grade SDK test coverage.

Background: Current SDK tests exercise synchronous calls and VCR-style replay. We need deterministic streaming tests that can emulate partial frames, intentional backpressure, connection interruptions, and recoverable errors so we can assert correct SDK retry/backoff, event ordering, KV cache warmup behavior, and user-facing streaming APIs (async iterators, callbacks, readable streams).

Deliverables:
- A lightweight mockserver (Go binary + Docker image) that supports: deterministic stream chunking, configurable delays/backpressure, injected network errors (reset, timeout), header validation, and an assertion endpoint to validate received request metadata (model, prompt, max_tokens, streaming flag).
- A compact fixture format (JSONL + metadata) for deterministic streaming traces that can be consumed by all three SDK test harnesses.
- Example test suites in: Python (pytest + asyncio), TypeScript (Jest + node streams), Go (testing + httptest) demonstrating: streaming consumption, retry-on-idempotent-chunk failures, resume semantics using resume tokens/KV cache hints, and proper propagation of partial results to user callbacks.
- CI job templates that run the mockserver and the three test suites in parallel (matrix coverage) and fail the build on any contract deviation.
- A small doc (Confluence) with guidelines for writing new streaming fixtures and for adding language bindings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Mockserver image published to internal registry (redwood/mockserver:eng-42711) and containerized run documented.
- Fixtures for at least 3 streaming scenarios (normal uninterrupted stream, intermittent chunk failure + retry, deliberate backpressure causing delayed chunks) committed under examples/fixtures/streaming/ with clear metadata.
- Passing test examples: python/tests/test_streaming_retry.py, ts/tests/streaming-retry.spec.ts, go/tests/streaming_retry_test.go in the repo.
- CI matrix runs these tests on pull requests touching SDK code and fails on contract diff.
- A follow-up issue template for adding new streaming fixture cases and for recording flaky behaviors to triage.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Mockserver will not attempt to fully emulate model logits; it will emit predictable token frames encoded as JSON with sequence IDs to make deterministic assertions easy. This keeps test fixtures small and deterministic.
- We'll implement backpressure by respecting a configurable read-window before sending the next chunk; this requires the SDK test client to simulate slow consumers in some tests.
- For retries: tests will validate that SDKs only retry on idempotent operations (stream reconnects that re-request continuation token) and that duplicate frames are deduplicated by sequence ID. If production introduces different resume semantics, fixtures will need updating.
- We will avoid expanding full VCR functionality in this ticket; the fixture format will be compatible with future record/replay work but stays intentionally minimal now.

Tasks (high level):
1) Mockserver core and docker image + config format (Rafael)
2) Fixture format spec + 3 canonical fixtures (Maya)
3) Python example harness + pytest examples (Emily Chen)
4) TypeScript harness + Jest examples (Alex Park)
5) Go harness + tiny httptest-based examples (Rafael)
6) CI job + matrix config and artifact upload for traces (SRE/CI)
7) Documentation and how-to (Confluence link)
8) Create follow-up tickets for: flaky incident tracking, extending resume token semantics, integration with existing VCR replay infra

Risks and mitigations:
- Flaky tests due to timing: mitigate by using deterministic fixtures and explicit timeouts; prefer logical sequence IDs over wall-clock timing where possible.
- SDK API mismatch: early prototype examples will be done for each SDK; if churn occurs we will gate merge with SDK API compatibility checks.
- Security: mockserver will run in CI-only private environment; no customer data used. Security review not required for this internal tool (marking as false) but if KMS or credential usage appears we will reopen review.

Related artifacts:
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Streaming+Mockserver+Design
- Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/980 (python harness prototype), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/981 (ts harness prototype)

Notes to reviewers: focus on the fixture schema and the resume/retry acceptance tests. If you think we should include a non-deterministic fuzzing stage, please call it out for a follow-up ticket.
